content: Insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (IDDM) is a term used to describe a form of diabetes mellitus that necessitates insulin therapy to prevent the development of ketoacidosis, a potentially life-threatening condition. While IDDM is frequently used interchangeably with juvenile diabetes mellitus and type 1 diabetes mellitus, these terms are not entirely synonymous. The term juvenile diabetes is now considered outdated and imprecise because type 1 diabetes can manifest in adults, and type 2 diabetes can also occur in children. IDDM primarily refers to type 1 diabetes, which is characterized by an absolute deficiency of insulin due to autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells. However, in some cases of type 2 diabetes, as the disease progresses, individuals may develop significant insulin deficiency that necessitates insulin therapy, thereby meeting the criteria for IDDM. For further clarification, refer to the definitions and distinctions of diabetes mellitus, type 1 diabetes mellitus, and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
